items.question: A utility cabinet pad on DOT right of way will stick up exactly 4 inches above the existing ground. Does the Utilities Accommodation Manual count that as an aboveground utility object?
items.note: UAM 3.3.2: anything extending above existing ground by 4 inches or more is an aboveground utility object, so exactly 4 inches counts (yes).

items.question: A new aboveground utility box 24 inches wide would block part of the line of sight at a commercial driveway. Would NCDOT permit it under the UAM?
items.note: UAM 3.3.3.1 item 10: a new or replacement aboveground installation that obstructs part of the line of sight of a highway or commercial driveway AND is more than 18 inches wide shall not be permitted -> no.

items.question: For an overhead utility crossing, how wide does a highway median have to be before poles or other aboveground facilities may be placed in it?
items.note: UAM 3.3.3.1 item 13: on crossings, aboveground facilities shall not be located in a median less than 80 feet wide.

items.question: How tall is the stub pole the UAM allows for mounting a small cell meter or power disconnect, typically?
items.note: UAM 3.3.6.3: a stub pole is typically 5 feet in height or less above ground and considered non-breakaway.

items.question: What's the highest BUG uplight rating a luminaire can have in a roadway lighting design on NCDOT right of way?
items.note: UAM 3.3.7.6: in no case shall luminaires with an uplight rating greater than 1 be used.

items.question: How far from the edge of travel do light poles on a controlled access L-line have to be installed?
items.note: UAM 3.3.7.13 Lighting within Controlled Access Right of Way: minimum of 15 feet from the edge of travel.

items.question: For an encased water main crossing a non-controlled-access road, how far does the UAM say the encasement has to extend?

all_of: 5 feet beyond the toe of slope

items.note: Missing variable: the roadway section type. UAM 3.4.3 minimum encasement extents: cut sections ditch line to ditch line; fill sections 5 feet beyond the toe of slope; curb and gutter sections 3 feet beyond the curb (and in every case beyond the 1:1 slope from the edge of pavement). Gas/fuel, controlled access and private-use liquid branches are excluded by the question.

items.question: A gas line casing under a state road will be exactly 150 feet long. Where do the vents go per the UAM?
items.note: UAM 3.4.3 vents: encasements 150 feet long and less get a vent on the high end; greater than 150 feet get vents on both ends. At exactly 150 ft: high end only.

items.question: What factor of safety does the UAM require for a restrained joint system that balances thrust forces at pipeline bends, tees and reducers?
items.note: UAM 3.4.5.1 Joint Restraint at Bends, Tees, and Reducers: restrained joint system factor of safety 1.25 for the test pressure. Near-identical to the joint restraints (fittings) bullet on p. 106 (safety factor 2): this item asks about the restrained joint system design.

items.question: If joint restraints are used on water main fittings, what safety factor does the UAM's acceptable pipe materials list require for them (not the restrained joint system design)?
items.note: UAM p. 3-33 fittings: joint restraints (if used) minimum working pressure rating of 200 psi with a safety factor of 2. Near-identical to the restrained joint system factor 1.25 on p. 105.

items.question: Under 'Unsuitable Pipe Materials' in the UAM, which PVC pipe is barred from NCDOT right of way for pressure uses like water lines and force mains?
items.note: Heading wording from the contents (3.4.6 Unsuitable Pipe Materials ... 3-34, p. 4); answer on the content page: PVC SDR 26 pipe will not be allowed for pressure applications.

items.question: What is the maximum operating pressure for HDPE plastic natural gas pipe in the UAM's acceptable materials?
items.note: UAM 3.4.5.3 Natural Gas: HDPE SDR 11.5, PE3408 and PE2406, maximum operating pressure 60 pounds per square inch gauge.

items.question: A brick utility manhole will be exactly 12 feet deep. What minimum wall thickness does the UAM call for?
items.note: UAM 3.4.8.2: for depths up to, but not exceeding, 12 feet: 8 inches for brick (6 for block); greater than 12 feet: 12 inches. Exactly 12 ft -> 8 inches.

items.question: What's the minimum wall thickness for a concrete block utility manhole under the UAM?
items.note: Missing variable: manhole depth. UAM 3.4.8.2: depths up to and including 12 feet -> 6 inches for concrete block; deeper than 12 feet -> 12 inches.

items.question: When does a tunnel liner plan have to show the shortest distance between the proposed tunnel and an existing highway structure? Within what distance?
items.note: UAM 3.4.10.2 plan view: required if any portion of the proposed tunnel is 200 feet or closer to any portion of an existing highway structure.

items.question: How far horizontally does an underground utility have to stay from the nearest part of a bridge per the UAM?
items.note: Missing variable: installation method. UAM 3.5.2.2 Bridges and Retaining Walls: open cut -> minimum 5 feet horizontally; HDD -> minimum 10 feet horizontally.

items.question: If a utility is bored and jacked under the bottom slab of a box culvert, how deep below the slab does the top of the encasement have to be?
items.note: UAM 3.5.2.2 Reinforced Concrete and Structural Plate Culverts: if the boring and jacking method is used, the top of the encasement is at a minimum depth of 1 foot below the bottom slab (and extends 10 feet beyond).

items.question: When a utility is buried in the fill over a concrete culvert, how close can it get to the inside face of the headwall?
items.note: UAM 3.5.2.2: at least 18 inches from the inside face of the headwall.

items.question: What grout mix ratio does the UAM call for to fill voids found outside a bored-and-jacked encasement pipe?
items.note: UAM 3.6.8.1: voids filled with 1:3 portland cement grout through grout holes at 10-foot centers.

items.question: Who has to investigate and approve vegetation cutting or trimming tied to a utility encroachment before the agreement gets final approval?
items.note: UAM 3.6.14.2. The same sentences appear in the TSLG guide (tmsd, L18_TSLG_Guide.pdf p. 552), checked with shared.py; gold is the utilities page.

items.question: Roughly how wide is a microtrench cut for fiber, per the UAM's shallow trenching section?
items.note: UAM 3.7.1: macrotrenching 12-36 in deep, up to 3 in across; microtrenching 6-12 in deep, usually 1.25 inches across; nanotrenching about 2 in deep, under 1 in wide. Near-identical list; the question names microtrenching.

items.question: Under the UAM's 'Failure to Comply' provisions, if a utility won't pay NCDOT's invoice for removing its facilities, who does NCDOT refer the matter to?
items.note: Contents entry 4.1.7 Failure to Comply ... 4-4 (p. 5); content page p. 147: refer to the Office of the Attorney General. Same passage in the TSLG guide (tmsd, L18_TSLG_Guide.pdf p. 554).

items.question: Under 'Utilities on Subdivision Roads', how many lots does a subdivided tract need for its road to count as a subdivision road?
items.note: UAM 2.4.15 (contents p. 3 lists it at 2-27): subdivided into two or more lots. The same definition is in the TSLG guide p. 570 and the Policy on Access Manual p. 14 (tmsd).

items.question: How does the UAM glossary define fully controlled access? What does it prohibit?
items.note: Glossary A-3: fully controlled access prohibits crossings at grade or direct private driveway connections; the next entry (partial) allows some. Same sentence in C34 - Manual 2012.pdf p. 107 (tmsd).

items.question: Per the UAM glossary, above what phase-to-ground voltage does electric power count as primary service?
items.note: Glossary: primary service above 7200-volt phase to ground; secondary below.

items.question: A small water system serves exactly 15 customers. Is it a public utility under the UAM?
items.note: UAM 1.3.3.2: public utilities serve at least 15 customers (G.S. 62-3(23)a.2.) -> yes.

items.question: Which access control type in the UAM allows private driveway connections but typically still has a controlled access fence?
items.note: UAM 1.2.2: limited controlled access allows no private driveways; partially controlled access allows private driveways with fence typically present; non-controlled has no fence.

items.question: The UAM has a section on utility facilities not permitted in NCDOT right of way. Which sections does it point to for the complete list?
items.note: Contents entry 1.10 (p. 2); content page 1-11: see Sections 3.1.2.7 and 3.1.2.8.

items.question: List all the NCDOT publications the UAM names as relevant to utilities accommodation.

expected.value: Standard Specifications for Roads and Structures

items.note: UAM 1.15.5: five items on p. 1-13, three more on p. 1-14.

items.question: Under the DENR-DOT memorandum of agreement on encroachments for UST remediation effluent (UAM appendix), how much written notice must either agency give before withdrawing?
items.note: Scanned memo, no text layer, signatures over the text. Item (12): ninety (90) days prior to withdrawal.

items.question: Which North Carolina General Statute does NCDOT's gateway sign standard practice cite for its authority to control all signs in state highway right of way?
items.note: Standard Practice G-6 (modified 4/23/12), page 2 of 3, scanned with no text layer: G.S. 136-30 (a), (b), (d).

items.question: What date is on the Chief Engineer's memo about communication enclosures with power in the UAM memos?
items.note: Scanned memo with a RECEIVED stamp (MAY 11 2009) and a signature: the memo date is May 7, 2009, not the stamp date.

items.question: Under the 2009 guidance on communication enclosures with electrical power, which General Statute lets an applicant claim exemption from the PE-sealed safe location determination?
items.note: Scanned e-mail (June 8, 2009) with blurred lines: registered professional civil engineer unless exempt per General Statute 89C-25.

items.question: In the frac-out contingency plan included with the UAM's HDD requirements, within how many minutes must the vacuum truck be able to reach any point along the drill shot?
items.note: Scanned plan (no text layer), section 6.1 Vac-Truck: within 10 minutes of a frac-out.

items.question: What's the maximum spacing between right of way markers in the Roadway Design Manual's right of way chapter?
items.note: RDM Part II ch. 9, section 9-2 item 2 (section numbers, not page folios; the page prints no page number).

items.question: On a rural job, the area needed past a large drainage pipe for channel maintenance reaches exactly 75 feet from the parallel right of way line. Should it be bought as right of way or as a permanent drainage easement?
items.note: RDM 9-4: on rural projects this area should normally be purchased as regular right of way if it does not extend beyond 75 feet; beyond 75 feet consult the Right of Way Branch. Exactly 75 ft -> regular right of way.

items.question: A parcel totals 3.2 acres and one part of it is 0.06 acre. How should that part's area be shown on the right of way area data?
items.note: RDM 9-5A rule (2): parcel over one acre -> parts of 0.10 acre or more in acres, parts under 0.10 acre in square feet.

items.question: What parcel number series is used for advanced acquisitions in the Roadway Design Manual?
items.note: RDM 9-6: the Right of Way Branch assigns the parcel number using the 900 numerical series (901, 902, ...).

items.question: On the Roadway Design Manual's right of way Estimate Request Form, what has to be filled in for each alternate or section when the estimate is requested by alternates?
items.note: Estimate Request Form 9-9 F-1: alternate name or number, description, type of access control, proposed R/W dimensions.

items.question: Who assigns the right of way project number for a highway project?
items.note: RDM 9-10: the Project Management Unit assigns it when funds are authorized.

items.question: On partial control of access projects, what opening width is normally used when setting access point stations?
items.note: RDM 9-3: a width of 60 feet is normally used (not shown as a dimension on plans).

items.question: Under the 2026 cost reimbursement guidance flow chart, how long must a utility have held land by adverse possession to claim a compensable interest?
items.note: Flow chart (a picture; checked against OCR of the page). Missing variable: color of title. Adverse possession: 7 years under color of title, 20 years without color of title.

items.question: A utility's pole sits outside the existing DOT right of way and the utility holds a recorded easement. Under the 2026 cost reimbursement guidance, what will it be reimbursed for if NCDOT asks it to relocate?
items.note: Flow chart: outside existing ROW -> compensable interest -> recorded easement -> utility will be reimbursed for its non-betterment costs.

items.question: The UAM cites CI/ASCE 38-02 for subsurface utility data. Which edition of the ASCE standard guideline for investigating and documenting existing utilities does FHWA's EDC-8 SUE fact sheet cite?
items.note: Older edition 38-02 (2002) is cited in UAM p. 23 and hif22002.pdf p. 5; the EDC-8 fact sheet (2023) cites ASCE/UESI/CI 38-22, the current edition.

items.question: In FHWA's Delaware SUE tech brief, what size water line under a bridge slated for replacement was SUE expected to locate?
items.note: hif22002.pdf p. 4 Project Example: a 16-inch diameter water line beneath the bridge.

items.question: Per Table 4-8 of the FHWA Highway/Utility Guide (minimum clearance requirements under maximum sag conditions), what clearance may a service drop wire have over a residential driveway?
items.note: Table 4-8, row Residential driveways: clearance 15.5 ft, Remarks column: service drop wires may be 11.5 ft. Heading wording as in the list of tables (p. 15, "... 87"). Scanned page with an OCR text layer.

items.question: In the Highway/Utility Guide's sag clearance table, what minimum clearance applies to a line running along a rural light-traffic road where it is not back of an obstruction?
items.note: Table 4-8, group "Running along:", sub-row Rural (light traffic) roads: back of obstruction 9.5, not back of obstruction 13.0, public alleys 15.5 ft. Read off the image (text layer order is scrambled).

items.question: In the Highway/Utility Guide's minimum cover table for buried cable, how deep must fiber optic cable be under ditches?
items.note: Table 4-9 Minimum cover for buried cable (Depth of Cover in inches): fiber optic cable normal 36, under ditches 42.

items.question: If buried telephone cable has to be bonded, how close to the end of the cable route must a bond be placed according to the Highway/Utility Guide?
items.note: Two-column text below Table 4-9, list item (2): within 150 m (500 ft) of the end of the cable route.

items.question: In Table 4-5 of the Highway/Utility Guide, what is the longest available Class 2 pole if it is a jack pine (JP) pole?
items.note: Table 4-5 Characteristics of Poles: Class 2 longest available pole 125* ft; note *: the longest JP, LP, or NP pole is 60 feet. The note changes the value.

items.question: In the 1993 Highway/Utility Guide's table of authorization for accommodation of utilities by state, what does North Carolina's entry allow on other Federal-aid highways?
items.note: Table 8-1 (Continued), p. 155: NC row codes 1, 1, 1, X; legend 1 = Crossings only. The table starts on p. 154 (pdf 170); the NC row is on the continuation page.

items.question: How many utility pole fatalities did North Carolina have from 1980 to 1989 according to Table 9-2 of the Highway/Utility Guide?
items.note: Table 9-2 Utility Pole Fatalities by State for 1980-1989, three side-by-side state blocks; North Carolina: 80-89 = 393, max year 53.

items.question: For a rural collector with a design speed of exactly 40 mph, what horizontal clearance does the Highway/Utility Guide's table of 1990 Green Book clearances give?
items.note: Table 9-3, row 5 Rural collector with design speed: At or below 40 mph -> Min 10'; at or above 50 mph -> use Roadside Design Guide; between 40 and 50 -> desirable 50 mph widths.

items.question: In Table 12-1 of the Highway/Utility Guide, which categories of highway does Virginia's statute cover for reimbursing utility relocation?
items.note: Table 12-1 Statutory Authority Relating to Reimbursement of Public Utility Relocation Expense, last continuation page (printed 243-246, pdf 259-262); scanned with no text layer. Virginia (Code of Va. 33.1-44; 55; 56): X under Interstate Urban Only and State Highways.

items.question: Under the Indiana cut road permit special provisions reproduced in the Highway/Utility Guide, how thick must the bituminous base mixture in an asphalt pavement replacement be at least?
items.note: Appendix C sample permit form, scanned with no text layer, hand-drawn marks across paragraph (a) and sideways margin labels: pavement replacement not less than 12 inches of bituminous base mixture.

items.question: In that Indiana cut road permit, what is the maximum variation from vertical allowed on the edge of a removed concrete pavement area?
items.note: Paragraph (B): maximum variation from the vertical will not exceed 1 1/2 inches (printed with a half glyph; OCR reads it as "1/½2", so read off the image).

items.question: In Figure 10-6 (channelizing devices) of the Highway/Utility Guide, how tall must a Type III barricade be at minimum?
items.note: Figure 10-6 Channelizing Devices (source MUTCD Part VI), scanned with no text layer: Type III barricade 60" minimum (Types I and II 36").

items.question: Under 23 CFR 645.207, where does the clear zone start?
items.note: Two-column CFR page. Clear zone: total roadside border area starting at the edge of the traveled way. Same definition in the TMP Design Manual p. 25 (wztc) and in the 2003 reprint in if03014.pdf p. 91.

items.question: Which Executive Order makes private lines that drain adjacent wetlands onto Federal-aid highway right of way prohibited under 23 CFR 645?
items.note: 645.209(l) Wetlands, in the left column of a two-column page: inconsistent with Executive Order 11990, Protection of Wetlands (May 24, 1977), and prohibited.

items.question: How long are a utility's relocation cost records open to audit after it gets final payment, under 23 CFR 645 subpart A?
items.note: 645.119: subject to audit for a period of 3 years from the date final payment has been received by the utility. (23 CFR 710.201 has a separate 3-year retention rule for ROW records.)

items.question: Under 23 CFR 645.113, when can FHWA approve a lump-sum payment agreement for utility relocation without a later audit of actual costs?
items.note: 645.113(f): when the work for a specific utility can be clearly defined and the cost can be accurately estimated (both conditions).

items.question: How often must a State DOT's chief administrative officer certify to FHWA that its right-of-way manual is up to date, under 23 CFR 710?
items.note: 710.201(c)(2)(ii): every 5 years after the August 23, 2018 manual.

items.question: When FHWA gets a court order for possession in a direct Federal acquisition, 23 CFR 710 lets the applicant give owners 30 days' notice to vacate occupied properties. Is that right?
items.note: 710.603(d)(2): the right to give 90 days notice to owners to vacate occupied properties. The premise (30 days) is wrong.

items.question: On a Federal-aid project, when can authorization to advertise for bids be given, according to FHWA's companion guide on utility coordination and certification?

items.question: In the 2003 reprint of 23 CFR 645 in FHWA's Program Guide, item (iv) of 645.209(c)(2) is reserved. Under the item after it, who keeps control of the utility strip right-of-way?
items.note: Live text next to "(iv) [Reserved]" in Appendix B of if03014.pdf: (v) the State or political subdivision is to retain control of the utility strip right-of-way. (The 2024 CFR has the same item on its p. 14.)

items.question: Which edition of ASCE's subsurface utility data guidelines does FHWA's Delaware SUE case study list in its resources?
items.note: hif22002.pdf p. 5 Contacts and Resources: ASCE Standard Guidelines ... (38-02), 2002. The EDC-8 fact sheet in the same division cites the newer ASCE 38-22; the question names the document.

items.question: Per Roadway Design Manual chapter 18, when a project's utility impacts are rated high or medium, who should the Roadway Design Unit send the preliminary plans to?
items.note: 18-1 Coordination During Preliminary Design: plans go to the Utility Agent at the same time as to the Hydraulics Unit, then the Utility Conflicts Committee reviews them. "18-1" is a section number, not a page folio, so printed_pages is empty.

items.question: According to the utilities coordination and encroachments presentation notes, which two things decide which utility agreement a project needs?
items.note: Speaker notes for slides 9-10: "Explanation of the Various Agreements" (cont. next slide) ... "It depends on two things, whose cost and who's constructing." The answer sentence is on p. 10 only.
